successors.note: 'Noricum was incorporated into the Roman Empire in 16 BC' and became a province; divided into Noricum Ripense and Mediterraneum c. 296.

capitals.name: Noreia / Virunum on the Magdalensberg (Carinthia)
capitals.note: The Noricum page's intro puts the capital at 'the royal residence at Virunum on the Magdalensberg'; a later section says Noreia from 200 BC; the Noreia battle page puts it 'in the modern Carinthia' with the 'precise location unknown'. The point is the Magdalensberg (confidence 1).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Noricum row. The pages give no area; the five Austrian Laender come to about 65,000 km2 by the gazetteer (some of it north of the Danube), against 'most of modern Austria'. The Slovenian and Croatian fringes (the Kingdom page: 'parts of western Slovenia and a smaller part of northern Croatia') are not drawn. Soft edges.

ledger.note: 200 BC: the Norican tribes unite. 'From 200 BC, the Noricum tribes gradually united into a kingdom' with its capital at Noreia; the intro of the same page says 'The kingdom was founded around 400 BC' and the Kingdom of Noricum infobox gives 'c. 200 BC-c. 50 AD' with the founding field blank.

region.text: 'not far from Noreia in the modern Carinthia', where the Cimbri and Teutons reached the Danube in Noricum

ledger.note: 113 BC: the Cimbri and Teutons invade Noricum. They 'arrived at the Danube in Noricum, where the Taurisci could not repel them and so appealed to Rome'; Carbo's army is beaten 'not far from Noreia'. The pages do not say the invaders held ground; they 'headed west, towards Gaul'.

region.text: 'not far from Noreia in the modern Carinthia'

ledger.note: 113 BC: the Cimbri-Teutonic victory at Noreia, after which they 'headed west, towards Gaul' rather than invading Italy; Noricum's borders did not change.

region.text: 'most of modern Austria and part of Slovenia': the Danube to the north, Raetia and the Vindelici to the west, Pannonia to the east and south-east, Italy (Venetia et Histria) to the south; the Slovenian and Croatian fringes are not drawn

ledger.note: 16 BC: Noricum becomes a Roman province. 'Noricum was incorporated into the Roman Empire in 16 BC'; in that year the Noricans, joined by the Pannonians, invaded Histria and were defeated by Publius Silius Nerva, proconsul of Illyricum (the page then says Noricum 'became a Roman province'). The state had been 'a key ally of the Roman Republic' since before 113.

ledger.note: 16 BC: the Kingdom of Noricum ends; the province of Noricum is its successor.

wars.name: Battle of Noreia
wars.outcome: Cimbri-Teutonic victory over Papirius Carbo near Noreia; the invaders then went west to Gaul and Noricum kept its land; Carbo killed himself after Marcus Antonius prosecuted him.
wars.note: The Noricum page names the Teutones as the invaders; the Noreia page names the Cimbri, Teutons and Ambrones, with Noricum on the Roman side.

wars.name: Norican-Pannonian invasion of Histria (16 BC)
wars.outcome: The Noricans and Pannonians invaded Histria and were defeated by Publius Silius Nerva; Noricum was then incorporated as a province.
wars.note: No Norican land held beyond the frontier is recorded.

certainty.note: The Danube, Raetia, Pannonia and Italy are the limits the page gives; no survey or treaty line.

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria. Pages disagree on the founding (about 400 BC in the intro of Noricum, 200 BC in its history section, 'c. 200 BC' in the Kingdom infobox) and on the kingdom's end (the Kingdom infobox c. 50 AD, which is the province's early years; the Noricum page 16 BC). The Noricum page does not mention Caesar in 58 BC, King Voccio or Burebista; those, and the Boii in Noricum, are not recorded. The counterpart for the 16 BC loss is roman-empire (eu-04), as Cliopatria's Roman Empire row begins in -31; roman-republic's dossier has no Noricum event. Wikidata id left null. Family 'austria' is a registry key.
